declined.why: Refuted by the verifier and not applied. Substring containment at tools/validate_skills.py:412 is deliberate and documented twice: the module docstring says the rule fires when an -implement breakage 'repeats its ideal facet's word for word, or is wholly contained in it', and the comment at lines 401-405 says 'Only an outright copy is reported, since a genuinely escalated breakage ... is a legitimate second failure mode.' The scanner's own example, 'cache fails' inside 'cache fails permanently', is precisely the containment case the rule exists to catch. Reproduced over all 44 ideal/-implement pairs: 0 flagged, so no false positive exists today. It is also a warning, never an error. Tightening it to word-boundary or exact match would remove the only case it detects.

Refuted by the verifier and not applied. The docstring is on class OpenAICompatibleAdapter (examples/end-to-end/run.py:164-168), i.e. inside an adapter, which is exactly where this repo's rule puts product names: tools/validate_skills.py:315-325 flags PRODUCTS only outside a section whose heading starts 'Adapters', and F-part-c-09 says 'Products belong in the adapter column only.' The docstring itself de-pins the product: 'the product behind $GATEWAY_URL is replaceable without touching anything above. model = the profile's model_class, so the caller names a class, not a vendor.' Naming today's product in the adapter is the convention, not a leak.
